definitions.explanation: The act of fundamentally changing and renewing systems, institutions, or practices. Most famously associated with the Taika Reform ({大化|たいか}の{改新|かいしん}) of 645 CE, one of the most important events in early Japanese history.

examples.japanese: {制度|せいど}の{改新|かいしん}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: Reform of the system is necessary.

examples.japanese: {大化|たいか}の{改新|かいしん}は{日本|にほん}の{歴史|れきし}の{転換点|てんかんてん}だった。
examples.english: The Taika Reform was a turning point in Japanese history.

examples.japanese: {組織|そしき}を{改新|かいしん}して、{時代|じだい}に{合|あ}った{形|かたち}にする{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: We need to reform the organization and bring it into a form suited to the times.

notes:
Compound of {改|かい} (change, reform) and {新|しん} (new). Most strongly associated with {大化|たいか}の{改新|かいしん} (Taika Reform, 645 CE), which centralized political power under the emperor and is a key topic in Japanese history education.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大化|たいか}の{改新|かいしん}: the Taika Reform (645 CE)
- {制度|せいど}の{改新|かいしん}: institutional reform
- {改新|かいしん}を{行|おこな}う: to carry out reform

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {改革|かいかく}: reform — the most common modern word for reform, used broadly
- {刷新|さっしん}: renovation, overhaul — implies sweeping, dramatic renewal
- {革新|かくしん}: innovation, reform — emphasizes radical or progressive change
- {維新|いしん}: restoration, revolution — used historically ({明治|めいじ}{維新|いしん}, Meiji Restoration)
